name: b-camcorder-party-guest
prompt: A single paused frame of a family's taped home movie from around 1998, shot at a sitting-room party on a cheap handheld video camera. Crepe-paper streamers in mismatched colours sag from the ceiling corners, a trestle table under a paper cloth carries crisp bowls, cocktail sticks of cheese and pineapple, a jelly and a two-litre bottle of fizzy pop, and behind it relatives in patterned shirts and cardigans are caught dancing, arms up, smeared into soft ghosts by the slow shutter, one aunt laughing with her eyes shut. In front of all this, at waist height in the frame, stands a guest in a plain charcoal knitted ski mask and matching knitted gloves, every inch of skin covered except the eyes looking out through the two eye holes, the wool unmarked and plain. They hold a floppy white paper plate with one sausage roll on it, body still angled toward the buffet, head turned square to the lens, calm and courteous, as if waiting to be introduced. No one in the room has noticed them. The camera's own little lamp throws a hard flat wash straight onto the masked face so the knit and the eye holes read cleanly and evenly while the corners of the room fall into murky brown and tungsten orange; slight tilt and wobble from a hand-held grip, autofocus a touch soft, faint horizontal line texture and smeared reds of tape, lifted blacks, milky warm colour, highlights on the foil platters clipping white. Ordinary, cosy and happy, with one guest who should not be there. No writing, numbers, date stamp or lettering anywhere in the image.
